text:
emma: :rotating_light: seeing a big spike in streaming frame decode errors right after the canary rollout (client v12). Error rate ~4.8% of streaming requests, latency unaffected but streams aborting. Root traces point to frame encoding mismatch.
incident-bot: Alert: HIGH - streaming.frame.decode.errors on /v1/stream (svc-runtime). Triggered at thread_ts 3361112223.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy completed: release/sdk-client-v12 - canary percentage 5% - deploy_id=deploy_2026_03_15_21.
raj: ack - oncall here. Emma can you paste the top error lines and affected regions/pools?
emma: logs from the runtime:
```
E decoding frame: unknown encoding "gzip+v2" client=client-7f9e pool=gpu-west-1 stream_id=0x7a12
E stream aborted: frame decode failure, upstream code 1002
```
Most errors from gpu-west-1 and a few in eu-central. 5% traffic was on canary, but we've got downstream clients that send gzip+v2 frames; looks like the runtime drop-in didn't include the newer decoder shim.
lucas: that matches — build for v12 removed a soft-fallback for legacy gzip variants during the codec refactor. Canary introduced stricter validation.
sofia: Support: we already have two customers reporting aborted sessions (ids: CUST-998, CUST-1021). They're premium. Need communication.
maya: tagging product — we should escalate to SEs and runbook. Is this a kill-switch or rollback?
raj: initial plan: flip FF to disable v12 path for canary traffic (kill-switch) while we confirm. If that fails, roll back the canary. I'll try kill-switch first — less blast radius.
raj: toggling kill-switch now: `POST https://flags.redwood.internal/api/feature/sdk_v12_canary -> {"enabled": false}`
raj: (executed) feature flag updated. Observability: turning down.
emma: after kill-switch we see error rate drop to ~0.3% within 2 minutes. Confirming still some residual aborts probably from in-flight sessions.
deploy-bot: Canary traffic routed back to stable line for release/sdk-client-v12 (canary 0%).
janitor-bot: Note: canary rollback recorded in deployment log deploy_2026_03_15_21 -> rollback_3361112250.
lucas: we should push a hotpatch to re-add soft-fallback decoder ASAP. I can build a patch that reintroduces the compatibility shim, run a quick test, then re-enable canary.
zed: agree. But first: customers impacted list and comms. Sofia, can you own customer outreach?
sofia: on it. Sending proactive note to CUST-998 and CUST-1021, and a general incident banner for active sessions.
maya: severity: P1 given premium customer impact and streaming reliability. Assign postmortem.
emma: quick repro steps for devs:
```
echo -n "..." | ./rt-client --encoding gzip+v2 --stream https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream
# runtime logs show: unknown encoding 'gzip+v2'
```
Also a pointer to failing unit test in repo: `tests/codec/test_legacy_gzip.py` (skipped in v12).
lucas: I'll open a PR with the compatibility shim and mark it as hotpatch. ETA 30-45m for build+canary.
raj: handoff to next oncall @lucas in 45m. I'll stay until canary stable.
sofia: Comms sent to customers; interim note: "We're aware of streaming aborts for some sessions after a recent client compatibility change. We've disabled the canary and are rolling a compatibility hotpatch."
maya: please include estimated ETA for fix when available.
lucas: PR #4827 created: "reintroduce legacy gzip fallback". Running CI (smoke + codec).
lucas: smoke passed in staging. Planning to re-enable canary to 2% after deploy.
raj: re-enable canary to 2% now, monitor metrics closely.
emma: metrics: error rate down to baseline, small blips at 1.2% on-streams for a few minutes then back to 0.2%.
zed: good. Once canary at 2% stable for 15m, ramp to 5%.
raj: ramped to 5% at +35m, metrics look stable.
sofia: customers notified that sessions should be operational. They're verifying.
maya: action items for post-incident: 1) enforce codec E2E in canary test; 2) add enforcement in release checklist to validate soft-fallbacks; 3) update compatibility matrix docs; 4) customer impact blameless postmortem.
emma: logging followup: increase decoder-fallback log level and add an alert when decoding errors > 0.5% over 5m for streaming endpoints.
lucas: will add test and create a follow-up PR for test coverage and release notes.
zed: thanks team. tagging for postmortem owner: lucas. Closing incident thread once postmortem scaffolded. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident resolved: streaming.frame.decode.errors - mitigation applied (kill-switch + hotpatch + controlled canary). Resolution time ~40m after alert.
sofia: final note to customers dispatched with root-cause and ETA for postmortem.
---
Summary (for logs): - Cause: canary rollout removed legacy gzip compatibility fallback in runtime codec refactor. - Impact: ~4.8% streaming aborts during canary window affecting premium customers (2 confirmed). - Mitigation: feature-flag kill-switch -> rollback of canary -> hotpatch reintroducing shim -> controlled canary ramp. - Time to mitigation: ~40 minutes.
Action items (short): [lucas] hotpatch PR merged and tests added; [emma] update alerting; [sofia] customer comms archive; [team] postmortem scheduled.
